name: Carousel
summary: A row of cards or pictures that scrolls sideways, with previous and next buttons.
description:
Use a carousel for a set of similar items when space is short: testimonials, products, team members. If people need to compare or see everything, use a grid instead.

The track is a scroll-snap row, so swiping, trackpad scrolling and the arrow keys on the focused track work without JS. data-v-carousel shows the buttons, moves one slide per press and disables a button at its end. It never moves on its own. How many slides show follows the carousel's own width.

classes.name: v-carousel
classes.description: The wrapper, with aria-roledescription="carousel" and an aria-label. Set --v-per-view-sm, -md and -lg to change how many slides show at each width (defaults 1.15, 2.2, 3).

classes.name: v-carousel-track
classes.description: The scrolling list (<ul role="list">). Give it tabindex="0" and an aria-label so keyboard users can scroll it.

classes.name: v-carousel-slide
classes.description: One slide, an <li>. The JS labels it "2 of 5" unless it has a label.

classes.name: v-carousel-controls
classes.description: The button row, hidden until the JS runs.

states.description: Set on .v-carousel by the JS: the buttons are shown and the scrollbar is hidden.
Set on a button at its end of the track.

hooks.name: data-v-carousel
hooks.description: Shows the buttons, moves one slide per press (smoothly unless reduced motion is on), disables them at the ends and labels the slides.

hooks.name: data-v-carousel-prev
hooks.description: Moves back one slide. Its arrow flips in right-to-left.

keyboard.action: Reaches the track, the links inside the slides, then the buttons.
On the focused track, scrolls it; snapping lands on a slide.
On a button, moves one slide.

a11y: No autoplay, so nothing moves that the reader did not ask for (WCAG 2.2.2).
Every slide stays in the page and in the reading order; the buttons are a shortcut, not the only way to reach them.
Slides are labelled "2 of 5" with aria-roledescription="slide" so screen readers know where they are.

examples.title: Customer quotes
examples.description: Five quote cards; the buttons move one card at a time.
